category: CAM Processor, printing and manufacturing output
description: Producing output from EAGLE 9.6: printing drawings and texts to the system printer or PDF, the CAM Processor with JSON CAM jobs (Gerber RS-274X/X2, Excellon drill, BOM, pick-and-place, DXF), the Manufacturing flyout, headless generation with eaglecon -X, the legacy CAM Processor (INI jobs, output devices from eagle.def, aperture wheels, drill racks, tolerances, flags), outlines data for milling, and the CAM job files shipped with the installation.

tools.name: Print dialog (drawing)
tools.description: Appears for PRINT without a terminating ';' or for Print... in the Control Panel context menu of a drawing. It selects paper and orientation, preview, Mirror, Rotate (90 degrees), Upside down (180, or 270 together with Rotate), Black (ignore layer colours), Solid (ignore fill styles), a scale factor and a page limit (0 = unlimited; otherwise the scale is reduced until the drawing fits). For schematics it prints All, From...to or This sheet, and Hierarchy prints module sheets once per module instance with the instance's part and net names; Printer... opens the system printer dialog and PDF... writes a PDF with the same settings.
tools.usage: PRINT   (without ';')   |   Control Panel > right-click a .brd/.sch > Print...
tools.example: In the board editor: DISPLAY NONE 16 17 18 20; PRINT > Paper A4, Mirror off, Black, Solid, Scale factor 1, Page limit 1 > PDF... > demo2_bottom.pdf
tools.notes: The printout uses the white-background palette and only the layers currently displayed. Board polygons print in calculated form only after RATSNEST; SET DISPLAY_MODE NODRILL prints pads and vias without holes. Printing from the Control Panel prints the file as saved on disk.

tools.name: Print dialog (text)
tools.description: Printing a text file from the Control Panel context menu or the Text Editor's File menu opens a reduced dialog with 'Wrap long lines' plus the common page-setup fields. Printer... selects and configures the system printer and PDF... writes the text to a PDF file instead.
tools.usage: Control Panel > right-click a .ulp/.scr/.txt > Print...   |   Text Editor > File > Print
tools.example: Right-click bom.ulp > Print... > Wrap long lines on > PDF... > bom_listing.pdf

tools.name: Printer Page Setup
tools.description: Page placement options shared by the print dialogs. Border sets the left/top/right/bottom margins (defaults come from the printer driver; entering 0 uses the hardware minimum), Calibrate holds X (print-head direction) and Y (paper-feed direction) scale factors for exact 1:1 prints, Alignment positions the drawing on the sheet, and Caption prints date, time and file name (plus 'mirrored' and f=<scale> where applicable).
tools.usage: Print dialog > Border | Calibrate | Alignment | Caption   (command line: PRINT ALIGN TL; PRINT CAPTION;)

parameters.name: Border
parameters.description: Margins in mm or inch; values are enlarged automatically if a newly selected printer needs larger minimums.

parameters.name: Calibrate X / Y
parameters.description: Correction factors (default 1) determined by measuring a printed reference length.

parameters.name: Caption
parameters.description: Adds a caption line with time, date and file name.

tools.example: Print a 100 mm reference line, measure 99.8 mm in paper-feed direction > Calibrate Y = 1.0020; then always re-measure production prints.
tools.notes: The printed scale factor is shown with four decimals, so f=1.0000 may still not be exactly 1.0.

tools.name: CAM Processor
tools.description: EAGLE's manufacturing-data generator, reworked in 8.6. Started from the board editor it loads the current board, chooses a template job that fits the layer count and lists every output in an Output Files tree grouped by section (Gerber, Drill, Assembly, Drawing, plus Legacy for old jobs); selecting an item shows a preview and its settings. Process Job writes all outputs, Export File only the selected one, and 'Export as ZIP' packs everything into one archive.
tools.usage: Board editor > File > CAM Processor (or the CAM icon in the action toolbar, or MANUFACTURING CAM;)

parameters.name: Load job file
parameters.description: New CAM Job, open a .cam file or pick one of the examples; right-click Legacy to load an old-style job.

parameters.name: Select Board...
parameters.description: Process another board than the one in the editor; the status bar shows the board and its assembly variant.

parameters.name: Save / Save As / Edit Description...
parameters.description: Store the job as JSON .cam with an HTML description.

parameters.name: Units and format specifiers
parameters.description: Metric/imperial and integer/decimal digits per Gerber and drill section.

parameters.name: Export as ZIP
parameters.description: Write all outputs into a single ZIP archive.

tools.example: Load job file > examples > Third Party > OSH Park > OSHPark_2_layer.cam > inspect each item's preview > Process Job > choose the output folder.
tools.notes: Default formats: Gerber RS-274X for plots and Excellon for drills. Since 9.5.1 the processor warns when Gerber item layers do not match the board's layer stack, and it warns when the assembly variant matters for an output (BOM, pick and place, paste mask).

tools.name: Manufacturing flyout
tools.description: Opened by the MANUFACTURING command (board editor only, since 8.6). It shows the board through the manufacturer's eyes: a live board preview, drill information and board properties, with export of DXF and JPG/SVG drawings and a CAM button. MANUFACTURING CAM opens the CAM Processor and MANUFACTURING EXPORT immediately writes a ZIP archive with Gerber and Excellon data for the current design.
tools.example:
MANUFACTURING;          # toggle the flyout and check the drill tab
MANUFACTURING EXPORT;   # one-click Gerber + Excellon ZIP

tools.name: CAM job file (JSON)
tools.description: Since 8.6 a CAM job is a JSON document with the extension .cam. Its top level holds type ('EAGLE CAM job'), version, author, a per-language HTML description, timestamp, units ('metric' or 'imperial'), output_type ('directory' or 'zip') and an outputs array of sections; every section has an output_type of gerber, drill, assembly or drawing, optionally a filename_prefix, and its own outputs items.
tools.notes: Old INI-style jobs are still processed in the Legacy section. Out-of-range integer/decimal digit counts produce an error message. Easiest way to write a job: copy a shipped example_N_layer.cam and edit it.

tools.name: Gerber output section
tools.description: The section of a JSON CAM job that produces photoplot files. It sets the Gerber version (RS274X or X2), the coordinate format as integer and decimal digits, a filename_prefix that items reference as %PREFIX, whether a Gerber job file is generated, and the list of gerber_layer items. With generate_job_file the processor also writes gerber_job.gbrjob, a JSON summary with board size, thickness and layer count.
tools.example:
{"output_type": "gerber", "version": "X2", "filename_prefix": "gerber",
 "format_specifier": {"integer": 2, "decimal": 6}, "generate_job_file": true, "outputs": [ ... ]}
tools.notes: Since 9.2 the default for templates and new Gerber items is RS-274X, and a prefix naming a non-existent directory creates that directory.

tools.name: gerber_layer item
tools.description: One Gerber file in a job: the EAGLE layers merged into it, the file name pattern, the polarity and the X2 file-function configuration. The board_outline and milling flags add the board shape and cutouts (the templates' Profile item sets both), and advanced_options mirror, rotate or offset the image. The GUI's Negative polarity checkbox corresponds to polarity 'negative'; the GUI's Board shape and Cutouts checkboxes draw these edges 10 mil wide.

parameters.name: layers
parameters.description: EAGLE layer numbers, e.g. [1, 17, 18] for top copper with pads and vias, [21, 25] for top silkscreen, [29] for top solder mask.

parameters.name: board_outline / milling
parameters.description: Include the board shape / cutouts (the Profile items of the templates set both).

parameters.name: polarity
parameters.description: positive (default in all shipped jobs since 9.3) or negative image.

tools.example:
{"type": "gerber_layer", "name": "Silkscreen Top", "layers": [21, 25],
 "filename_format": "%PREFIX/silkscreen_top.gbr", "polarity": "positive", "board_outline": false, "milling": false,
 "config": {"file_function": "Legend", "index": 1, "layer_type": "top"},
 "advanced_options": {"mirror": false, "rotate": false, "upside_down": false, "offset_x": 0, "offset_y": 0}}
tools.notes: Since 9.5 layer presets can be selected for an item. Inner copper of a 4-layer EAGLE board usually lives in layers 2 and 15, so check the layer list against the Layers tab of the design rules.

tools.name: Gerber file function (config)
tools.description: The config object of a gerber_layer item describes what the file contains, which Gerber X2 writes as file attributes and the Gerber job file uses for the layer stack. file_function is Copper (with layer = position in the stack counted from the top, layer_type top/Inner/bottom and layer_details 'mixed'), Soldermask or Legend (layer_type and index), Paste (layer_type), Profile (plating 'plated' or 'non-plated') or Other (free description).
tools.notes: Before 9.3 some mask functions switched the output to negative polarity automatically; this no longer happens.

tools.name: Drill output section
tools.description: The section that writes Excellon drill data. An 'autodrills' item (Auto Drill, since 9.4) produces one file per via layer span found in the layer setup, named with %FROM/%TO; 'excellon' items instead name a layer span and choose which hole types to include, which is how plated and non-plated holes are split into separate files.

parameters.name: autodrills
parameters.description: filename_format such as %DRILLPREFIX/drill_%FROM_%TO.xln; drill_1_16.xln for a normal through-hole board.

parameters.name: excellon.drills
parameters.description: {"PTH": true, "VIA": true, "NPTH": false} - plated pads, vias and non-plated holes.

tools.example:
{"type": "excellon", "name": "Nonplated Drills", "layers": {"from": 1, "to": 16},
 "drills": {"PTH": false, "VIA": false, "NPTH": true}, "filename_format": "%N.nonplated.drills.xln"}
tools.notes: The processor warns if the Excellon configuration does not cover all drill sequences of the board's layer setup. Units follow the section/job setting (fixed in 9.4.1).

tools.name: Assembly output section
tools.description: Section for assembly data: a 'bom' item (since 9.4) writes a simple bill of materials and a 'pick_and_place' item (since 9.5) writes centroid files for the front and back side. Both respect the current assembly variant, and the templates put them in CAMOutputs/Assembly.
tools.example: Result for board Grov-Button-v1.0: Assembly/Grov-Button-v1.0.txt (Qty, Value, Device, Package, Parts, Description) plus PnP_Grov-Button-v1.0_front.txt and PnP_Grov-Button-v1.0_back.txt with lines like 'R2 4.45 7.87 90.00 10k 0603'.
tools.notes: For richer BOMs use bom.ulp; for other placement formats mount.ulp, mountsmd.ulp or mount-smd-tht.ulp.

tools.name: Drawing output section (DXF)
tools.description: Section for drawing exports; the shipped templates leave it empty except the 1-layer template, which contains a DXF item. The DXF item writes the board as a multi-layer DXF file and can place signals on individual layers.
tools.example: eaglecon -X -dCAMJOB -jexample_1_layer.cam -oD:\out board.brd   # writes CAMOutputs\DrawingFiles\board.dxf besides Gerber and drill data
tools.notes: DXF via -dCAMJOB works since 9.2 (earlier versions failed with 'unexpected condition'); dxf.ulp and cam2dxf.ulp are alternatives.

tools.name: CAM job file name placeholders
tools.description: Placeholders used in filename_format of JSON job items. %PREFIX, %DRILLPREFIX, %ASSEMBLYPREFIX and %DRAWINGPREFIX insert the filename_prefix of the Gerber, drill, assembly and drawing sections, %N the board name, %FROM and %TO the first and last layer of a drill span, and %BOARDSIDE the side of a pick-and-place file (front or back).
tools.example:
"filename_format": "%N.toplayer.ger"         -> board.toplayer.ger
"filename_format": "%DRILLPREFIX/drill_%FROM_%TO.xln" -> CAMOutputs/DrillFiles/drill_1_16.xln
tools.notes: The 6- to 16-layer templates use %PREFIX/%FF.gbr for every Gerber item; %FF is not documented in the help and evidently names the file after the item's function. Paths are relative to the output directory given with -o or chosen in the GUI.

tools.name: Advanced options (mirror, rotate, offset)
tools.description: Per-item geometric options of JSON CAM jobs: mirror, rotate (90 degrees), upside_down (180 degrees) and an X/Y offset. In the GUI the Mirror Horizontal, Mirror Vertical and Rotate buttons change colour when active so that a transformed output is not overlooked.
tools.example: "advanced_options": {"mirror": true, "rotate": false, "upside_down": false, "offset_x": 0, "offset_y": 0}   # mirrored bottom film
tools.notes: Board houses expect unmirrored, unrotated data in the board's own coordinates, so leave these off for normal fabrication outputs.

tools.name: Gerber RS-274X and Gerber X2
tools.description: RS-274X (extended Gerber) embeds the aperture definitions in each file and is EAGLE's default Gerber format; the default template format is 3.4 metric, i.e. 0.0001 mm resolution. Gerber X2 adds attributes that state each file's function, layer position and polarity so that the board house can identify the files automatically. The older RS-274D format needs a separate aperture wheel file and is only available through the legacy devices GERBER and GERBERAUTO.
tools.example:
Header of an EAGLE RS-274X file (example_2_layer.cam):
G04 EAGLE Gerber RS-274X export*
%MOMM*%
%FSLAX34Y34*%
%INTop Copper*%
%IPPOS*%
tools.notes: Some services did not accept X2 when the third-party jobs were written (the Seeed Fusion jobs deliberately use RS-274X); check what your fabricator wants. Excellon drill data default to 3.3 mm with leading zeros suppressed.

tools.name: eaglecon -X -dCAMJOB
tools.description: Processes a complete JSON CAM job from the command line without opening the editors or signing in: Gerber files, the Gerber job file, drill files, BOM and pick-and-place and DXF are written below the output directory according to the job's prefixes. Combine with -N for silent batch runs, -A for an assembly variant and -U- to ignore personal settings.
tools.example:
"C:\Program Files\EAGLE 9.6.0\eaglecon.exe" -X -N -dCAMJOB -j"C:\Program Files\EAGLE 9.6.0\examples\cam\examples\example_2_layer.cam" -oD:\out\rev_A D:\Work\board.brd
# -> D:\out\rev_A\CAMOutputs\GerberFiles\copper_top.gbr ... gerber_job.gbrjob, DrillFiles\drill_1_16.xln, Assembly\board.txt, PnP_board_front.txt
tools.notes: Verified on 9.6.0 in September 2026 without an Autodesk sign-in (a few seconds for a small board). Since 9.5 a missing output folder is created; paths with spaces must be quoted.

tools.name: eaglecon -X -dGERBER_RS274X
tools.description: Legacy single-output mode: renders the listed layers of a board with one eagle.def device into one file. This is how pre-8.6 batch files produced a Gerber set, one call per film, and it still works for quick checks or unusual layer combinations.
tools.example:
eaglecon -X -dGERBER_RS274X -oD:\out\board.cmp D:\Work\board.brd 1 17 18
eaglecon -X -dGERBER_RS274X -oD:\out\board.stc D:\Work\board.brd 29
eaglecon -X -dGERBER -Waperture.whl -oboard.sol -D-0.1 board.brd 16 17 18
tools.notes: Layers may be given by number or name (e.g. pad via bottom). The manual's own example swaps the labels of the .cmp/.sol lines; layer 1 is the component (top) side.

tools.name: eaglecon -X -dEXCELLON
tools.description: Legacy Excellon drill output from the command line. Layers 44 (Drills: plated pads and vias) and 45 (Holes: non-plated HOLE objects) go into one file with the drill table in its header, and a .dri info file is written alongside; boards with blind/buried vias get one file per via span.
tools.example:
eaglecon -X -dEXCELLON -oD:\out\board.drd D:\Work\board.brd 44 45
eaglecon -X -dEXCELLON -oD:\out\board_pth.drd D:\Work\board.brd 44
eaglecon -X -dEXCELLON -oD:\out\board_npth.drd D:\Work\board.brd 45
tools.notes: EXCELLON writes inch units (2.5 format); use EXCELLON_33MM for millimetres or edit eagle.def. A warning about drills and holes in one file can be silenced with SET Warning.Cam.DrillsAndHolesConcurrent 0.

tools.name: Legacy CAM Processor main menu
tools.description: The menu of the classic CAM Processor window as documented in the help. File opens a board for processing, a drill rack or aperture wheel file for editing, or another job, and saves the job; Layer deselects all layers or shows only the selected or all layers. Window switches to the Control Panel or the editors, and Help has pages for the CAM Processor, jobs and devices.
tools.usage: CAM Processor (legacy) > File | Layer | Window | Help
tools.example: File > Open > Job... > gerb274x.cam; File > Open > Board... > demo2.brd; Process Job.

tools.name: Legacy CAM job sections
tools.description: A legacy CAM job consists of sections, each a complete parameter set (device, output file, layers, flags). The Section selector switches between them, Prompt defines a message shown before a section runs (e.g. 'Please change paper!'), Add creates a section from the current settings, Del removes one, Process Section runs the current one and Process Job runs all in order.
tools.usage: Section selector | Prompt | Add | Del | Process Section | Process Job
tools.example: Add 'Component side' (GERBER_RS274X, %N.cmp, layers 1 17 18), Add 'Solder side' (%N.sol, 16 17 18), then Process Job.
tools.notes: Add a new section before changing parameters; changing first and then adding asks whether the current section's modifications should be saved.

tools.name: Legacy CAM job file format
tools.description: Pre-8.6 .cam files are INI-style text. A [CAM Processor Job] block holds language-specific descriptions and the list of sections; each [Sec_n] block stores Name, Prompt, Device, Wheel, Rack, Scale, Output, Flags, Emulate, Offset, Sheet, Tolerance, Pen, Page, Layers and Colors.
tools.usage:
[CAM Processor Job]
Description[en]="..."
Section=Sec_1

[Sec_1]
Name[en]="..."
Device="GERBER_RS274X"
Output="%N.cmp"
Layers=" 1 17 18"
tools.example:
[Sec_1]
Name[en]="Generate drill data"
Device="EXCELLON"
Scale=1.000000
Output="%N.drd"
Flags="0 0 0 1 0 1 1"
Tolerance="0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.025000 0.025000"
Layers=" 44 45"
tools.notes: Flags holds seven 0/1 values corresponding to the flag options (shipped jobs use "0 0 0 1 0 1 1": positive coordinates, optimize and fill pads on). Such jobs appear under Legacy in the 9.x CAM Processor.

tools.name: Output Device
tools.description: Chooses the legacy output device and its main files. Device lists all drivers from eagle.def; Scale enlarges or shrinks on scalable devices, and a negative value limits the output to that many pages; File, Wheel and Rack take full names or just an extension (e.g. .gbr, .whl, .drl) that is appended to the board name.
tools.usage: Legacy CAM Processor > Device | Scale | File | Wheel | Rack   (command line: -d, -s, -o, -W, -R)
tools.example: Device EXCELLON, File .drd   (-> board.drd; the Rack field is hidden because EXCELLON builds its drill table itself)
tools.notes: Page limiting with a negative scale needs correct Width/Height for the device (dialog fields or eagle.def).

tools.name: Aperture Wheel File
tools.description: For RS-274D photoplotters a wheel file assigns D-codes to aperture shapes and sizes (round, square, rectangle, oval, draw). Several apertures may share one D-code if they are of type draw or round and have the same size, which maps apertures that draw identically to a common code.
tools.usage: D<code>  <type>  <size> [x <size2>]   (select with -W<file> or the Wheel field)
tools.example:
D010    round     0.004
D040    square    0.004
D100    rectangle 0.060 x 0.075
D104    oval      0.030 x 0.090
D110    draw      0.004
tools.notes: GERBERAUTO generates a wheel automatically; the GLASER device uses the shipped glaser.whl. RS-274X devices embed apertures and need no wheel.

tools.name: Aperture Emulation
tools.description: When enabled, apertures missing from the wheel are drawn with smaller available apertures; when disabled no emulation takes place. Emulation can make photoplotting very slow and therefore expensive.
tools.usage: Legacy CAM Processor > Emulate Apertures   |   -e / -e+ (on), -e- (off, default)
tools.example: eaglecon -X -dGERBER -Wmywheel.whl -e -oboard.cmp board.brd 1 17 18

tools.name: Aperture Tolerances
tools.description: Percent tolerances for draw and flash apertures: if no aperture of the exact size exists, one within the tolerance is used. Allowing tolerances may break the design rules, so keep them small.
tools.usage: Legacy CAM Processor > Tolerance Draw/Flash   |   -D<tol> (draw), -F<tol> (flash); 0.1 = 10 %, +/- prefix for one direction
tools.example: eaglecon -X -dGERBER -Waperture.whl -D-0.1 -F+0.05 -oboard.sol board.brd 16 17 18

tools.name: Drill Rack File
tools.description: Drill stations that cannot generate their own tool table need a rack file assigning tool codes to diameters. It is typically created with drillcfg.ulp (RUN drillcfg in the board editor, units mm or inch) and passed to devices such as EXCELLON_RACK, SM1000 or SM3000; the board house then also needs this .drl file.
tools.usage: T<nn>  <diameter>   (select with -R<file> or the Rack field)
tools.notes: The EXCELLON family writes the drill table into the drill file header, so no rack is needed there.

tools.name: Drill Tolerances
tools.description: Percent tolerance for drill diameters: if the rack has no tool of the exact size, a tool within the tolerance is used. It only matters for drill devices that work from a rack file; devices that build their own tool table (EXCELLON family) use the exact diameters.
tools.example: eaglecon -X -dEXCELLON_RACK -Rboard.drl -E0.05 -oboard.drd board.brd 44 45
tools.notes: The shipped excellon.cam stores drill tolerances of 0.025 (2.5 %) in its Tolerance field.

tools.name: Offset, printable area and pen data
tools.description: Device parameters for plotters and printers. The X/Y offset in inches moves the origin (e.g. to the plotter's lower left corner), and the printable Width and Height in inches define the page; if the rectangle around all objects (even those not output) does not fit, the drawing is split into several parts. For pen plotters the pen diameter in mm is used to hatch filled areas and the pen velocity is given in cm/s (0 = plotter default).
tools.example: eaglecon -X -dHPGL -x0.5 -y0.5 -w15 -h10 -p0.3 -v0 -oboard.plt board.brd 16 17 18 20

tools.name: eagle.def
tools.description: The text file (in the installation's bin folder) that defines all legacy output devices. Each [NAME] section starts with a Type (PenPlotter, PhotoPlotter, DrillStation, Generic, Calcomp or CalcompE) and sets strings and numbers such as Long, Init, Reset, ResX/ResY, Width/Height, Move/Draw/Flash, AutoAperture, AutoDrill, Units and Decimals; '@NAME' inherits another definition (up to 10 levels). To add a driver, copy a similar section, rename it and change only the differing parameters, using an editor that inserts no control characters.
tools.example:
[GERBER_RS274X_MM]
@GERBER_RS274X_33MM
Long = "Company Gerber RS-274-X, 3.3 mm"

[EXCELLON]
...
Units = mm      ; drill table in millimetres instead of inch
tools.notes: Units accepts Inch, MM or Auto and controls the units in the .gpi/.dri info files and generated tables; eaglecon -d? lists all defined devices.

tools.name: Output file names and placeholders (legacy)
tools.description: Legacy output file names can be typed literally or built from placeholders: %N board name, %E its extension, %P its directory, %H the home directory, %L the layer range of blind/buried drill files, %D{xxx} text only in the data file name, %I{xxx} text only in the info file name, and %% a percent sign. Conventional extensions are .cmp (top copper 1 17 18), .ly2/.ly3... (inner layers), .sol (bottom 16 17 18), .plc/.pls (silkscreen 21 25 / 22 26 with 20), .stc/.sts (stop masks 29/30), .crc/.crs (cream 31/32) and .drd (drills 44 45).
tools.example: %N.cmp%I{.info}   -> board.cmp (data) and board.cmp.info (info file)
tools.notes: Placeholders must be upper case. Make every section's extension unique so that no output overwrites another.

tools.name: Drill files for blind and buried vias
tools.description: If a board uses blind or buried vias, the CAM Processor writes one drill file per via length actually used, appending the start and end layer to the name (board.drd.0104 for layers 1-4, .0116 for through holes, pads and HOLEs). With %L the layer range can be placed elsewhere in the name; a single drill info file lists all generated drill files.
tools.example: eaglecon -X -dEXCELLON -oD:\out\hdi.%L.drd hdi.brd 44 45   # -> hdi.0102.drd, hdi.0215.drd, hdi.1516.drd, hdi.0116.drd
tools.notes: Existing files that match the pattern but are not produced by the current run are deleted first. In JSON jobs, Auto Drill items do the same with %FROM/%TO.

tools.name: Flag options
tools.description: Legacy output switches: Mirror, Rotate (90 degrees) and Upside down (180) transform the output and normally need 'pos. Coord' to avoid negative coordinates; pos. Coord shifts the drawing to the device origin; Quickplot draws only outlines; Optimize orders plotter moves; Fill pads fills pads (only on generic devices such as PostScript, otherwise drill holes stay visible).
tools.usage: -m (mirror, off)  -r (rotate, off)  -u (upside down, off)  -c (positive coordinates, on)  -q (quickplot, off)  -O (optimize, on)  -f (fill pads, on)
tools.example:
eaglecon -X -dPS -m -c -oboard_bottom.ps board.brd 16 17 18 20
eaglecon -X -dEPS -f- -oboard_top.eps board.brd 1 17 18 20   # show drill holes

tools.name: Layers and Colors
tools.description: In the legacy CAM Processor the layers to output are ticked in the layer list, and for colour-capable devices a colour number can be entered per layer. On the command line the layers follow the board file name, and for pen plotters -P assigns pens to layers.
tools.usage: Layer list checkboxes + Color field   |   eaglecon ... board.brd <layers>   |   -P<layer>=<pen>
tools.example: eaglecon -X -dHPGL -P1=1 -P16=2 -P20=3 -oboard.plt board.brd 1 16 20
tools.notes: Only the Vias layer (without a signal layer) outputs all vias; together with a signal layer on a blind/buried board only the vias of that layer are drawn.

tools.name: Outlines data
tools.description: Isolation-milling contours for prototype boards are computed from a special polygon: name _OUTLINES_, the only object of signal _OUTLINES_, Rank 6, Width equal to the milling tool diameter and large enough to cover the board. RATSNEST then calculates its contours as the tool paths and its fill as the area to clear, and outlines.ulp (or mill-outlines.ulp) extracts the data as script, HPGL or other formats.
tools.usage: POLYGON _OUTLINES_ <tool width> ...; CHANGE RANK 6; RATSNEST; RUN outlines [device [width [layer [filename]]]]
tools.notes: Check with a DRC whose clearances between different signals are at least the tool diameter; Isolate helps when milling sequentially with several tools. Delete the _OUTLINES_ polygon afterwards - it ignores the design rules and would short signals.

tools.name: GERBER_RS274X
tools.description: Legacy extended-Gerber devices that generate their apertures automatically (they inherit from GERBERAUTO) and embed them in each file. GERBER_RS274X uses the 2.5 inch coordinate format; the variants GERBER_RS274X_24 (2.4 inch), GERBER_RS274X_26 (2.6 inch) and GERBER_RS274X_33MM (3.3 mm) differ only in format and units.
tools.example: eaglecon -X -dGERBER_RS274X_33MM -oD:\out\board.GTL board.brd 1 17 18
tools.notes: Octagons are written with an aperture macro (OC8); eagle.def notes that a circle can be substituted for viewers that cannot handle it. An info file (.gpi) describes format and units.

tools.name: GERBER / GERBERAUTO
tools.description: Legacy RS-274D photoplotter devices. GERBER needs a wheel file listing the apertures, while GERBERAUTO builds a wheel automatically (D-codes from 10 upward); GERBER_23 and GERBERAUTO_23 use the 2.3 inch format. The shipped gerber.cam first runs GERBERAUTO over all layers to create the wheel and then GERBER for each film.
tools.example:
eaglecon -X -dGERBERAUTO -oboard.$$$ board.brd 1 16 17 18 20 21 25 29 30
eaglecon -X -dGERBER -Wboard.whl -oboard.cmp board.brd 1 17 18
tools.notes: Aperture tables are in inches by default; set Units = mm in the [GERBER] or [GERBERAUTO] section of eagle.def if the board house requires millimetres.

tools.name: EXCELLON
tools.description: Excellon drill-station devices that write the tool table into the drill file header (automatic tool numbers T01, T02 ...). EXCELLON uses the 2.5 inch format; EXCELLON_24 (2.4 inch), EXCELLON_26 (2.6 inch) and EXCELLON_33MM (3.3 mm) are format variants, and EXCELLON_RACK uses a user-supplied rack file instead of an automatic table.
tools.example: eaglecon -X -dEXCELLON_33MM -oD:\out\board.drd board.brd 44 45
tools.notes: A .dri info file is written with each drill file. The manual shows how to derive a leading-zero variant (EXCELLON-LZ) in eagle.def.

tools.name: PS / EPS
tools.description: Generic PostScript devices: EPS writes Encapsulated PostScript in editor coordinates on a virtually unlimited page, PS writes printable PostScript for a 7.75 x 11 inch area, PS_INVERTED an inverted (negative) printable version and PS_DINA3 printable PostScript for DIN A3. Because they are generic devices, Fill pads works correctly with them.
tools.example:
eaglecon -X -dEPS -oD:\out\board_top.eps board.brd 1 17 18 20
eaglecon -X -dPS -s2 -oD:\out\board_x2.ps board.brd 21 25 20
tools.notes: For documents PRINT FILE .pdf is usually simpler; the legacy layout2.cam and schematic.cam jobs use EPS.

tools.name: SM1000 / SM3000 / SMS68 / GBRDRL
tools.description: Further legacy drill-station devices: Sieb & Meyer 1000 (1/100 mm) and Sieb & Meyer 3000 (1/1000 mm), SMS68, and GBRDRL, which writes drill positions as Gerber drill codes (2.3 inch). They need a drill rack file, typically produced with drillcfg.ulp.
tools.example:
RUN drillcfg;   (board editor, save board.drl)
eaglecon -X -dSM3000 -Rboard.drl -oboard.sm3 board.brd 44 45
tools.notes: The manual lists SM1000/SM3000 as supported for legacy CAM jobs only.

tools.name: HPGL and pen-plotter devices
tools.description: eagle.def still defines many pen plotters and HP-GL printers: HPGL (16 x 11 inch), HPGLX (with Xon/Xoff), HPGL2 (HP-GL/2 printer), DESIGNJET220, DESIGNJET650, HPPJETXL300C, CALCOMP, CALCOMPE, CALCOMP_M84 and plotters such as CX6000, DXY800, DPX2200, ADCOMP, ADCOMP300, WX4671, HPX84, YEWPL, MP1000, EPSONHI80, SWEET, TEWIP281, SE281, RY10MZ, HIDMP and SPL10. HP-GL output is also a practical vector format for engravers and simple milling tools.
tools.example: eaglecon -X -dHPGL -P16=1 -P20=2 -p0.25 -oD:\out\board_bottom.plt board.brd 16 20
tools.notes: Page size defaults come from Width/Height in eagle.def (16 x 11 inch for most plotters).

tools.name: EMMA / GLASER
tools.description: Two legacy photoplotter devices defined in eagle.def: EMMA (EMMA 30/80 photoplotter) and GLASER (GLASER DP-1504 photoplotter). GLASER references the aperture wheel glaser.whl, which ships in the legacy CAM examples folder.
tools.example: eaglecon -X -dGLASER -W"C:\Program Files\EAGLE 9.6.0\examples\cam\examples\Legacy\glaser.whl" -oboard.cmp board.brd 1 17 18

tools.name: example_N_layer.cam
tools.description: Autodesk's default JSON CAM jobs for 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 and 16 copper layers (examples\cam\examples, version 9.2.0, metric). Each writes RS-274X Gerbers in 3.4 format with a Gerber job file to CAMOutputs/GerberFiles (copper, profile, solder mask, paste and silkscreen per side), an Auto Drill item to CAMOutputs/DrillFiles, BOM and pick-and-place files to CAMOutputs/Assembly, and an (empty, or DXF for 1 layer) drawing section.
tools.usage: CAM Processor > Load job file > examples > example_<N>_layer.cam   |   eaglecon -X -dCAMJOB -jexample_<N>_layer.cam ...
tools.example: eaglecon -X -N -dCAMJOB -j"C:\Program Files\EAGLE 9.6.0\examples\cam\examples\example_4_layer.cam" -oD:\out D:\Work\board4.brd   # inner copper from layers 2 and 15
tools.notes: The 4-layer job maps inner copper to layers 2 and 15, the 6-layer job to 2, 3, 14, 15, and the 16-layer job uses all layers 1-16; make sure your board's layer setup matches. The 1-layer job outputs top copper only.

tools.name: aisler_2_layer.cam / aisler_4_layer.cam
tools.description: Third-party JSON jobs for the AISLER prototype service (8.6.0 format). They write Gerber X2 files in 2.6 metric format into a 'gerber' folder (output.toplayer.ger, output.internalplane1.ger, output.topsoldermask.ger, output.boardoutline.ger ...), separate plated (PTH + vias) and non-plated Excellon files, and pack everything into a ZIP.
tools.example: eaglecon -X -dCAMJOB -j"C:\Program Files\EAGLE 9.6.0\examples\cam\examples\Third Party\AISLER\aisler_2_layer.cam" -oD:\out\aisler board.brd

tools.name: BetaLayout_N_layer.cam
tools.description: Third-party JSON jobs (2, 4 and 6 layers, 8.6.1 format) that generate production data for Beta Layout's PCB-POOL service into an 'outputs' folder. They use Gerber X2 with file function 'Other' and PCB-POOL extensions: .BS/.LS top/bottom copper, .il2/.il3 inner layers, .RBS/.RLS solder masks, .TPOS/.BPOS silkscreen, .SPT/.SPB paste, .CON profile (layers 20, 45, 46), plus one Excellon .drd with all hole types.
tools.example: eaglecon -X -dCAMJOB -j"C:\Program Files\EAGLE 9.6.0\examples\cam\examples\Third Party\Beta Layout\BetaLayout_4_layer.cam" -oD:\out\pcbpool board.brd

tools.name: OSHPark_2_layer.cam / OSHPark_4_layer.cam
tools.description: Third-party JSON jobs for OSH Park's 2- and 4-layer services, with imperial units and ZIP output. Gerbers are X2 in 3.6 format named %N.toplayer.ger, %N.internalplane1.ger, %N.topsoldermask.ger, %N.topsilkscreen.ger, %N.toppaste.ger, %N.boardoutline.ger etc.; drills are split into %N.plated.drills.xln and %N.nonplated.drills.xln (2.4 inch format).
tools.example: eaglecon -X -dCAMJOB -j"C:\Program Files\EAGLE 9.6.0\examples\cam\examples\Third Party\OSH Park\OSHPark_2_layer.cam" -oD:\out\oshpark board.brd

tools.name: SeeedFusion_2_layer.cam / SeeedFusion_4_layer.cam
tools.description: Third-party jobs for the Seeed Fusion PCB service (2018, 8.6 format). They deliberately use Gerber RS-274X instead of X2 and Protel-style names: .GTL/.GBL copper, .GTS/.GBS masks, .GTO/.GBO silkscreen, .GTP/.GBP paste, .GML mechanical (Dimension 20 + Milling 46, including board shape), .GL2/.GL3 inner layers in the 4-layer job, and one Excellon .TXT with plated and non-plated holes.
tools.example: eaglecon -X -dCAMJOB -j"C:\Program Files\EAGLE 9.6.0\examples\cam\examples\Third Party\Seeed Fusion\SeeedFusion_2_layer.cam" -oD:\out\seeed board.brd
tools.notes: The 2-layer job writes a ZIP, the 4-layer job a directory; the 4-layer inner layers are taken from EAGLE layers 2 and 15.

tools.name: gerb274x.cam
tools.description: The classic legacy extended-Gerber jobs for the GERBER_RS274X device. gerb274x.cam has six sections for a 2-layer board (.cmp, .sol, .plc, .pls, .stc, .sts), and gerb274x-4layer.cam adds inner layers 2 and 15 (.ly2, .l15) plus cream frames (.crc, .crs). gerb274x-mill-drill.cam uses GERBER_RS274X_26/EXCELLON_26 and adds a milling file (.mil, layer 46) and separate plated (.dpv, layer 44) and non-plated (.drh, layer 45) drill files.
tools.usage: examples\cam\examples\Legacy\gerb274x.cam | gerb274x-4layer.cam | gerb274x-mill-drill.cam (load under Legacy in the CAM Processor)
tools.example: CAM Processor > right-click Legacy > load gerb274x.cam > Process Job   (writes board.cmp, board.sol, board.plc, board.pls, board.stc, board.sts and a .gpi info file)
tools.notes: gerb274x.cam has no cream (paste) sections; use the 4-layer or mill-drill variant, or a JSON job, when SMD stencil data are needed.

tools.name: gerber.cam / excellon.cam
tools.description: Legacy jobs for older manufacturing flows. gerber.cam produces RS-274D data: its first section runs GERBERAUTO over layers 1 16 17 18 20 21 25 29 30 to create the aperture wheel, then GERBER writes .cmp, .sol, .plc, .stc and .sts. excellon.cam writes one Excellon drill file %N.drd from layers 44 and 45 with the tool table in the header (plus a .dri info file) and also handles blind/buried via spans.
tools.example: Legacy > excellon.cam > Process Job   -> board.drd + board.dri
tools.notes: excellon.cam does not separate plated and non-plated holes; use a JSON job with two excellon items or gerb274x-mill-drill.cam when the fabricator needs NPTH separately.

tools.name: layout2.cam / schematic.cam
tools.description: Legacy jobs using the EPS device, intended as input for the cam2print ULP (their descriptions call it cam2printer.ulp), which converts a CAM job into PRINT commands. layout2.cam has two sections for top (layers 1 17 18 20) and bottom (16 17 18 20) of a 2-layer board; schematic.cam outputs a schematic to %N.eps.
tools.example: RUN cam2print "C:/Program Files/EAGLE 9.6.0/examples/cam/examples/Legacy/layout2.cam" PDF
tools.notes: cam2dxf.ulp and cam2image.ulp convert CAM jobs into DXF or image exports in the same way.
